candidate.answerReason: The common chord equals the radius r of the circle with the 60-degree minor arc. A perpendicular construction in the other central triangle gives r^2=(2-sqrt(3))R^2, so the larger-to-smaller area ratio is 2+sqrt(3).

methods.label: Relate both radii to the common chord
methods.explanation:
The chord \(AB\) belongs to both circles, so it can connect their radii. Let \(O\) be the center of the circle with the \(30^\circ\) minor arc and let its radius be \(R>0\). Let \(P\) be the other center and its radius be \(r>0\). Arc measures give
\[
\angle AOB=30^\circ,
\qquad \angle APB=60^\circ.
\]
Because \(PA=PB=r\), triangle \(APB\) is isosceles with a \(60^\circ\) vertex angle, hence equilateral. Therefore \(AB=r\).

To find the same chord using \(R\), drop a perpendicular from \(B\) to the line \(OA\), meeting it at \(H\). The acute angle at \(O\) puts \(H\) on ray \(OA\). In right triangle \(OBH\), the side opposite \(30^\circ\) is half the hypotenuse, so
\[
BH=\frac R2,
\qquad OH=\sqrt{R^2-\left(\frac R2\right)^2}
=\frac{\sqrt3 R}{2}.
\]
Since \(OH<R=OA\), the point \(H\) lies between \(O\) and \(A\). Thus \(AH=R-\frac{\sqrt3 R}{2}\). Applying the Pythagorean theorem to \(AHB\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
r^2=AB^2
&=\left(R-\frac{\sqrt3 R}{2}\right)^2
  +\left(\frac R2\right)^2\\
&=(2-\sqrt3)R^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
The factor \(2-\sqrt3\) is positive and less than \(1\), so \(R>r\). Circle areas are \(\pi\) times the squared radii, hence the required ratio is
\[
\frac{\pi R^2}{\pi r^2}
=\frac1{2-\sqrt3}
=\boxed{2+\sqrt3},
\]
which is choice D.
